episode.title: Restore persisted conversation context when starting a new session
episode.before: At parent 1098b428e6e118be2e4ebb49a3dd2b14ae79e50e, coder initialization accepted optional in-memory completed messages but otherwise initialized an empty completed-message list. Although chat transcripts were persisted as Markdown, startup did not read or reconstruct that transcript, so a restarted session lacked prior conversational context. History summarization always used the model-defined history budget and could pass an arbitrarily large old-message head to the summarizer.
episode.after: At merge commit 45b2ba8a1056bb27f197b01d08f3ea0d4d92b668, initialization preserves explicitly supplied completed messages, but when none exist it reads the configured chat-history file, parses persisted user and assistant turns, installs them as completed messages, and starts background compaction. Startup announcements report restored history. A command-line token-budget override is propagated to the summarizer, and the summarization path selects the newest portion of an old-message head that fits within the summarizer model's input capacity.
episode.diff: Relative to first parent 1098b428, four implementation files changed: aider/args.py adds --max-chat-history-tokens; aider/main.py passes that option into coder construction; aider/coders/base_coder.py selects the configured or model-default budget, conditionally restores persisted history when no completed messages were supplied, starts summarization, and announces restoration; aider/history.py extracts Markdown-to-message parsing into ChatSummary and bounds the old-message subset submitted for summarization. No test file changed in the first-parent diff.

evidence_units.claim: The pinned ref is merge commit 45b2ba8a with first parent 1098b428 and subject 'Restore prior chat history on launch'.

Before the change, coder initialization converted an absent completed-message argument into an empty list and constructed ChatSummary from the model default, but performed no persisted-history read or restoration.

After the change, coder initialization uses an explicit history-token budget when supplied, otherwise the model default; if completed messages are empty, it reads io.chat_history_file, parses nonempty content, assigns the reconstructed messages, and invokes summarize_start().

The Markdown parser ignores transcript headings, quoted/tool output, and slash-command headings; it emits user messages from ordinary '#### ' headings and buffered assistant text as assistant messages.

When summarizing an oversized history head, the implementation walks backward from the newest old messages and retains only a subset within the summarizer model's maximum input tokens minus a 512-token reserve.
The command-line parser defines --max-chat-history-tokens with a null default, and the main construction path passes its value to the coder.
The startup announcement list includes 'Restored previous conversation history.' whenever completed messages are present after initialization.
The first-parent implementation diff changes only aider/args.py, aider/coders/base_coder.py, aider/history.py, and aider/main.py; it contains no test-file modification.
The complete first-parent patch passes Git's whitespace-error check.
The before/after diff adds persisted-history restoration without replacing explicitly supplied completed messages because the file read is guarded by an empty completed-message predicate.

before: At parent c4ea996612b23c6824089eb929caef43b0d4e880, AIAgent.run_conversation assigned `messages = conversation_history or []`. after: At 56b53bff6e42a534c7b9558b09aa28a6876e37d3, run_conversation creates a new outer list with `list(conversation_history)` when history is present. Existing message dictionaries remain shallowly shared.
diff: The implementation changes conversation initialization from direct aliasing (`conversation_history or []`) to a shallow list copy (`list(conversation_history) if conversation_history else []`). A regression test supplies a two-message history, runs one additional turn with a mocked response, asserts that the input list retains its original length, and asserts that the returned message list contains additional messages.

episode.title: Preserve caller-owned conversation history while resuming an agent conversation
episode.before: At parent c4ea996612b23c6824089eb929caef43b0d4e880, AIAgent.run_conversation assigned `messages = conversation_history or []`. When a non-empty history list was supplied, `messages` referenced the caller's list. The method then appended the new user message and subsequent generated messages to that same list, so resuming a conversation changed caller-owned state.
episode.after: At 56b53bff6e42a534c7b9558b09aa28a6876e37d3, run_conversation creates a new outer list with `list(conversation_history)` when history is present. The run can append new user and assistant messages to its working history and return the expanded transcript without changing the length of the caller's original list. Existing message dictionaries remain shallowly shared.
episode.diff: The implementation changes conversation initialization from direct aliasing (`conversation_history or []`) to a shallow list copy (`list(conversation_history) if conversation_history else []`). A regression test supplies a two-message history, runs one additional turn with a mocked response, asserts that the input list retains its original length, and asserts that the returned message list contains additional messages.

evidence_units.claim: Pinned merge commit 56b53bff6e42a534c7b9558b09aa28a6876e37d3 has first parent c4ea996612b23c6824089eb929caef43b0d4e880 and states that PR #229 fixes #228 by copying conversation_history to avoid mutating the caller's list.
The parent implementation initialized the working transcript as `messages = conversation_history or []`, causing a supplied non-empty list and the working transcript to be the same list object.

After initialization, run_conversation constructs the current user message and calls `messages.append(user_msg)`, demonstrating an in-place mutation of the working transcript immediately during a resumed turn.
The pinned change replaces the aliased initialization with `messages = list(conversation_history) if conversation_history else []` and documents that the copy prevents mutation of the caller's list.

The changed method still reads the original conversation_history to hydrate resumable todo state, while additions are made to the copied `messages` list; therefore prior state remains available without extending the caller-owned container.

TestConversationHistoryNotMutated.test_caller_list_unchanged_after_run passes a two-entry history to run_conversation, mocks a completed assistant response, and records the input list's original length.
The regression oracle asserts both sides of the ownership contract: the caller's history length remains unchanged and the returned run history is longer than the supplied history.
Relative to the first parent, the scoped resolution changes two lines in run_agent.py and adds a 33-line regression-test section in tests/test_run_agent.py.

The GitHub evidence bundle identifies repository NousResearch/hermes-agent, issue 228, linked PR 229, and the same mutation-avoidance resolution, but reports issue body, comments, timeline, PR body, reviews, and status checks as unavailable.

episode.title: Publish session forks and torn-tail repairs atomically
episode.before: At parent fadb74f684aaa7755463593e0564b58f9ed081e2, torn-tail recovery rewrote the live session file directly with its valid prefix. Forking created the destination header first and then appended copied entries, lane pointers, the session name, and labels one mutation at a time. A failure during either operation could therefore expose a damaged existing session or a discoverable partial fork.
episode.after: At a838c069e6318edee8317eff759b74c3934745f0, the filesystem abstraction supports atomic rename-and-replace. Forks and torn-tail repairs construct a complete sibling temporary file and publish it with one rename; failures remove the temporary file while leaving the destination absent or unchanged. Fork snapshot mutations are generated centrally from session state and reused by memory and JSONL storage.
episode.diff: Added a rename operation to the execution environment; added a stage-then-rename publication helper; routed torn-tail repair and JSONL fork creation through atomic publication; moved fork selection and mutation sequencing into the session-state owner; reduced the repository layer to path/header preparation and storage delegation; added failure-injection tests for staging, rename, repair, append-queue recovery, and replay validation.

evidence_units.claim: Commit a838c069e6318edee8317eff759b74c3934745f0 is the implementation-bearing resolution for PR/issue 7707 and has parent fadb74f684aaa7755463593e0564b58f9ed081e2.
The parent implementation repaired a torn final JSONL mutation by writing the valid prefix directly to the live session path.

The parent fork implementation created the destination session before copying entries, lanes, name, and labels through separate awaited appends, allowing intermediate destination states to become visible.
The new publication helper populates a deterministic sibling .tmp file, atomically renames it over the destination, and removes the temporary file on population or rename failure.
Torn-tail recovery now stages the valid prefix and publishes it through the atomic replacement helper instead of rewriting the live file directly.
Fork creation builds a temporary target containing the header and all selected mutations, publishes it atomically, and reloads the committed destination.
Session state now computes the complete ordered fork mutation sequence for tree or branch scope, including lane pointers, name, and labels, with fresh consecutive sequence numbers.
The repository prepares the destination identity and delegates fork publication to the source storage, while ordinary creation delegates file initialization to storage.
The execution environment implements rename-and-replace and reports a failed rename against the source path.
Filesystem tests verify that rename removes the source, replaces an existing destination, preserves the destination when the source is missing, and reports the missing source path.
Failure-injection tests verify that failed fork staging or failed atomic rename publishes no fork and leaves no temporary file.
A failure-injection test verifies that interrupted torn-tail staging preserves the original session bytes and removes the temporary file.
Fork conformance assertions verify that a reopened fork retains selected entries, lanes, name, and labels and excludes operation records.
An append failure test verifies that failed durable append does not advance in-memory state or poison the serialized write queue; the next append commits with sequence one and survives reopening.

The change modifies ten agent implementation and test files, adding 407 lines and removing 126 lines, with commit messages explicitly describing crash-safe JSONL publication and relocation of file creation, forking, and fork mutation construction.

semantic_action.pre_state: The dispatcher has selected a workspace runtime and explicitly configures one session service with its root, but bridge load/resume and other nested storage consumers run without a pinned ambient context.
semantic_action.post_state: The coordinated protocol restore and its bridge operations execute with the selected runtime root as the pinned ambient storage base directory.
semantic_action.validation: For both session/load and session/resume, activate a runtime replacement with a distinct root, store the target there, invoke the protocol request, and assert successful restoration plus the replacement root observed inside the bridge restore function.

candidate_workflows.name: preserve-selected-runtime-context-across-session-restore
candidate_workflows.description: After routing a restore request to a workspace-specific runtime, propagate that runtime's storage root across the entire asynchronous restore boundary for every exposed restore entry point, then verify load and resume against deliberately distinct roots.

workflow_graph.goal: A cold session load or resume consistently reads and reconstructs state from the storage root owned by the runtime selected for the request.
workflow_graph.entry_state: Multiple workspace runtimes may use distinct storage roots; request routing selects the correct runtime, but one or more restore entry points do not preserve its ambient storage context through asynchronous bridge restoration.
workflow_graph.exit_state: Every changed restore entry point encloses its full coordinated restore callback in the selected runtime's pinned storage context, and load/resume tests demonstrate that bridge code observes the selected non-default root.
unresolved_or_deferred: The two implementation steps are independent parallel repairs for separate entry points; the evidence does not establish a required ordering edge between them.

candidate_atomics.description: Execute the complete route-based cold load/resume operation inside the storage context owned by the selected workspace runtime.

semantic_action.intent: Prevent route-based session restoration from reading or creating runtime artifacts under a different workspace's or process-default storage root.
semantic_action.pre_state: A request has resolved a workspace runtime, but its coordinated restore callback and bridge load/resume execute without that runtime's pinned ambient storage context.
semantic_action.post_state: All storage resolution performed during the coordinated route restore, including asynchronous bridge work, observes the selected runtime's session storage root.
semantic_action.validation: For both cold load and cold resume, persist the target only under a distinct secondary runtime root, invoke the route, assert a successful response, and assert that the bridge observes that root through Storage.getRuntimeBaseDir().

call_sites: The route-based restore path now calls runWithWorkspaceRuntimeStorage(runtime, () => archiveCoordinator.runSharedMany(...)), placing session lookup, metadata recovery, bridge load/resume, relocation, and reconciliation within the selected runtime's pinned storage context.

The protocol dispatcher now defines restoreInRuntime for the coordinated restore operation and invokes it with runWithWorkspaceRuntimeStorage(sessionRuntime, restoreInRuntime), thereby enclosing bridge loadSession/resumeSession and related restore work in the selected runtime context.
tests: The route-level parameterized test writes a session under a secondary runtime root, invokes both cold load and cold resume through the session route, spies on the selected bridge operation, and asserts that Storage.getRuntimeBaseDir() observed during restoration equals secondaryRuntimeBaseDir and that the response succeeds.

The protocol-level parameterized test writes a session under a replacement runtime root, activates a replacement workspace runtime using that root, invokes session/load and session/resume, and asserts inside the bridge restore function that Storage.getRuntimeBaseDir() equals replacementRuntimeBaseDir; it also checks a successful result and one restore invocation.
